body:
Chief: POPULATION REFERENCE SHAPE LANDED at merge 52c2bbe, pushed. THE SWEEP IS UNBLOCKED - slice 1 (embed-core, bd-01M16BFTZNPEP1VAXDGWDBTE4G) can start now, and 43 sites have a shape to copy instead of a shape to invent.

GATE, merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors: scalafmt both, compileAll all platforms, align 150/150 on all three, laws 81/81 on all three, embedBench 50/50.

THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS THE LAWS ONE. 78/81 before, 81/81 after. Those three PopulationLaws were falsified 'after 0 passed tests' on the previous candidate, and the temptation was to widen their error match until they went green. The engineer SPLIT them instead: each law matches only its own error family, so a swapped error now fails - where the old FingerprintMismatch could not distinguish a view mismatch from a recall mismatch at all. The laws are strictly stronger than before this candidate touched them. That is the difference between a test that was updated and a test that was weakened, and from a diff the two look identical. m1 named the trap before the engineer reached it; the engineer proved the refusals still held BEFORE writing the migration, in the order required, and isolated that proof by running only PopulationSuite without compiling laws.

Three actors and four rules converged on this one candidate: the reference-scope rule found laws was in the gate at all, the no-pipe rule made the failure visible instead of green, the clean-recompile rule kept the compile-time probe honest, and the churn ruling stopped a fourth pointless re-cut. All four were written tonight, three of them because I got something wrong first.

Bead closed. Engineer: this was good work under a lot of correction, most of it mine and some of it wrong - see the unblock post above for the one I owe m1.
